# Draft:Germany and the 2026 Iran war

Background and Germany–Iran relations
Sanctions against Iran
As a member of the European Union, Germany was part of the union's sactions of Iran due to criticisms of human rights violations, with the Federal Government of Germany stating in a press release their support for the EU's sanctions.
Iranian Revolutionary Guard Designation as a Terrorist Organisation
On the 19th Febuary 2026, after the killing of protesters during the protests in Iran that started in December 2025, Germany designated the Iranian Revolutionary Guard as a terrorist organisation, and supported the European Union listing the IRGC as a terror group.
German Involvement in Middle East Missions
Counter Daesh/Capacity Building Iraq/NATOMission Iraq
The Bundeswehr is part of the "Counter Daesh/Capacity Building Iraq/NATOMission Iraq", an international mission in Iraq and  Jordan to combat the Islamic State, with between 200 and 500 German soliders involed in mission.
United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL)
The Bundeswehr is part of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), with 200 German soliders and a German navy frigate securing Lebanon's maritime borders as part of the UN peacekeeping mission.
Diplomatic Reponse
Government Reaction and Position
Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that he was informed in advance and that deliberations were underway in a joint statement with France and the UK. Addressing concerns over the legality of military action against Iran, Merz acknowledged a "dilemma", noting that decades of reliance on international law and sanctions had proven "clearly ineffective" against the Iranian government. On 1 March, Merz labelled the Iranian government as a 'terrorist regime' responsible for decades of domestic oppression, stating that Germany shares the goal of the United States and Israel to end its 'terror'.  On 24 March 2026, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier described the U.S.–Israeli military campaign against Iran as a "politically disastrous mistake" and a "violation of international law."
Military Reponse
Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Germany
Presence of German soldiers at sites attacked by Iran
During the war US military bases were targeted, one such military base that was hit was located near Erbil in Northern Iraq, and was where the Bundeswehr was stationed, yet the attack resulted in no deaths or injuries among the Bundeswehr.
Evacuation of German nationals
German charted flights to evacuate German nationals from the region, with an estimated 30,000 citizens stranded in the region.  The first flight to reach Germany being an Airbus A340-300 operated by Lufthansa, arriving in Frankfurt from   Muscat, the capital of Oman.  Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said vulnerable groups, such as pregnant women, the sick, and children, were prioritized for evacuation.
